bull.b: The sharp 2026 revenue and profitability rebound demonstrates strong operating leverage and demand recovery across the business. If elevated margins persist, substantially higher earnings and internal cash generation can support investment, product development, and shareholder returns over the next several quarters.

Multi-year New Business Models provide greater revenue visibility than spot NAND sales and deepen strategic relationships with datacenter and Edge customers. Their increasing share of bits through FY2028 could make the portfolio more predictable and support durable growth if contractual commitments are fulfilled.

Strong cash conversion combined with very low leverage gives SanDisk substantial financial flexibility. A conservative balance sheet can help fund capacity and technology ramps, absorb industry volatility, and continue capital returns without relying heavily on external financing.

bear.b: The recent turnaround follows a multi-year period of losses and volatile margins, showing that SanDisk remains exposed to NAND pricing and demand cycles. This history makes current earnings power less certain and raises the risk that profitability could contract materially when industry conditions weaken.

Persistent supply allocation may limit SanDisk’s ability to convert strong customer demand into additional shipments and revenue. Although scarcity can support pricing, constrained availability can also restrict growth, complicate customer commitments, and leave performance dependent on successful capacity expansion.

The shift toward large, long-term NBM agreements improves visibility but concentrates revenue and execution exposure among fewer strategic customers. Changes in customer demand, purchasing plans, or relationship quality could therefore have an outsized effect on future volumes and financial results.
